title: Zero Contact
premise: A glowing energy core drifts through a dark neon field while hostile red breach shapes close in from every edge. The player survives by steering the core away from contact for as long as possible.
interaction_model: Real-time pointer or touch dragging controls a smoothly drifting player orb on a full-screen arena. The input sets a movement target, and the orb eases toward it rather than moving instantly.
objective: Avoid touching any incoming enemy and survive as long as possible to increase your score.
progression: The run starts calm and becomes harder over time as enemies spawn more frequently and move faster. Progression is endurance-based rather than level-based, ending instantly on contact.
theme: Abstract sci-fi cyber defense with a containment-breach framing.
mood: Tense, sleek, reactive, and arcade-like, with neon glow effects and warning feedback.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy quick arcade survival challenges, mobile-friendly dodge games, minimalist skill games, and neon sci-fi presentation.
confidence_notes: High confidence in survival-dodge gameplay, pointer/touch movement, and score-over-time progression because these are explicit in code.
High confidence that the game is single-screen and replay-focused with no upgrades, weapons, or level structure.
Moderate confidence in thematic interpretation; the containment and breach fiction is inferred mainly from UI text and visual style.
recreation_prompt: Create a full-screen HTML5 arcade survival game called "Zero Contact" set in a dark neon sci-fi arena. The player controls a glowing cyan energy core in the center of the screen using mouse movement on desktop and drag/touch on mobile, with the core smoothly easing toward the current input point rather than snapping instantly. The goal is simple: survive as long as possible without touching any red hostile breach shapes that spawn from random screen edges and travel inward. Display survival time as the score in a compact HUD. Start with a menu screen that explains the rule in one sentence and lets the player begin immediately, then show a game-over panel with the final survival score and a replay button after collision. Make the difficulty ramp continuously by increasing enemy spawn rate and movement speed over time. Add a proximity warning system so that when enemies get dangerously close, a warning sound and a temporary animated overlay appear. Visually, use a polished cyber-arcade style with deep navy and black gradients, subtle grid and scanline effects, a glowing cyan/purple player orb with a trailing afterimage, pulsing red enemy forms, and a small particle burst on death. Include background music, UI click and start sounds, warning and defeat effects, and a mute toggle. Keep the game focused on one elegant survival loop with no weapons, levels, inventory, or upgrade systems—just movement, avoidance, rising pressure, and instant replayability.
